title: Lab 04 — Webhook Receiver: Signatures, Replays, Duplicates & Disorder

variants.hint: Every test you wrote sends a CORRECT signature. What should happen when someone who doesn't know the secret calls this endpoint?
variants.debrief: The receiver accepted any request, signed or not -- anyone on the internet could mark orders paid. Negative tests (wrong secret, tampered body) are the only way to see a missing security check, because the happy path looks identical.

variants.hint: A valid signature on an old message is still an old message. Can you sign something with a timestamp from ten minutes ago?
variants.debrief: The timestamp was signed but never checked for age, so a captured request could be replayed forever. Your signer taking the timestamp as a parameter is what made this testable.

variants.hint: Payment providers deliver the same event more than once. What should the SECOND delivery change?
variants.debrief: Each delivery of the same event fulfilled the order again. Deliver the same event id twice and assert fulfilments is still 1.

variants.hint: Read R4 again, word by word: what status must a duplicate delivery get?
variants.debrief: Duplicates were rejected with 409. That sounds safe, but any non-2xx tells the provider delivery FAILED, so it keeps retrying the event you already processed. A duplicate must be acknowledged with 2xx.

variants.hint: Events don't always arrive in the order they happened. Send the refund first.
variants.debrief: A late 'payment.succeeded' overwrote an earlier 'payment.refunded', flipping a refunded order back to PAID and fulfilling it. State transitions must not simply follow arrival order.
